text: Digoxin acts as a selective inhibitor of the **Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase (ATP1A1)** by binding to the extracellular domain of the α-subunit, specifically stabilizing the E2-P conformational state and preventing ion transport. This inhibition increases intracellular Na⁺ concentration, which subsequently reduces the activity of the Na⁺/Ca²⁺ exchanger (NCX), leading to elevated intracellular Ca²⁺ levels and enhanced myocardial contractility (positive inotropy). In the context of **heart failure**, this mechanism improves cardiac output and hemodynamics, while the drug's high affinity for the enzyme also modulates vagal tone to slow the heart rate. Consequently, Digoxin serves as a therapeutic agent to manage symptoms and improve clinical stability in patients with reduced ejection fraction and atrial fibrillation.
